question: Why is contrastive learning important in modern self-supervised learning?
direct_answer: It provides a way to learn useful representations from unlabeled data by using pairwise similarity as supervision.
expanded_answer: Modern self-supervised learning depends on creating a training signal without human labels. Contrastive learning does that by constructing positive pairs and comparing them against other examples. This makes it a strong foundation for representation learning at scale, especially when annotations are expensive or unavailable.
key_points: Key building block in self-supervised representation learning
common_wrong_ideas: Self-supervised learning means no training signal at all
Contrastive learning only matters for one specific model family
Unlabeled data cannot produce useful features
